courses.title: Fire & Life Safety Awareness
courses.campaignTitle: Notice the Risk. Prepare the Exit.

missions.title: Notice what normal hides
missions.purpose: Notice a hazardous condition while staying within a safe observation role.
missions.knowledge: Explain the source distinction between an ordinary object and the condition that makes it risky; recognise the five source hazard groups and the heat/fuel framing.
missions.skill: Observe a supplied scene and justify two priority observations.
missions.desire: Connect one ordinary routine to a person or responsibility the learner cares about, privately and without guilt.
missions.action: Complete one low-risk observation exercise and identify a specific issue for safe follow-up.

blocks.heading: Notice what normal hides
body: Your job is to notice, not to investigate a dangerous object. What would deserve attention before the next ordinary evening?
Choose a private observation in an already safe, accessible area or the equivalent fictional household exercise. Both are valid ways to practise.

blocks.heading: Keep observation low risk
body: Observe from a safe position. Do not move or test suspect objects, touch suspect electrical equipment, produce smoke, light anything or enter danger.
Keep household details on your own paper. You do not need to name people, share a home layout or upload a photo.

blocks.heading: Name the condition
body: An observation needs more than the name of an ordinary object. Describe the condition or arrangement that makes it deserve attention.
Separate what the scene shows from what you do not know. A useful explanation connects a visible condition with a reason to follow up.

blocks.heading: Choose two observations
body: In the fictional household scene, choose two observations and explain why each deserves attention.
Describe the condition attached to each observation. When the scene changes, look again and reconsider your priorities.

blocks.heading: Connect it to an ordinary responsibility
body: Which everyday responsibility makes this worth noticing? Think privately; you do not need to enter anyone’s name.

blocks.heading: Observe and choose a follow-up
body: Complete your safe observation or the fictional observation-and-recheck exercise. Privately note two observations and one specific follow-up.
The performed observation is the Action. Planning to look later is a next step, not completion of this task.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: What did you overlook at first?
What changed your priority?
What will you notice differently next time?

actionInstructions: Choose the safe-area observation or reviewed fictional scene.
Observe without moving, touching or testing suspect objects. Stop the real-world exercise if staying within this boundary is not possible.
Privately note two conditions, explain why they deserve attention and identify one follow-up within the awareness boundary.
For the fictional route, complete the changed-scene recheck as well as the first observation.
Consider the private review and choose one improvement.
aarPrompts: What did you overlook at first?
What changed your priority?
What will you notice differently next time?
reviewNotes: DRAFT — safety publication approval has not been granted. No completion-awarding checkpoint is supplied by this content asset.
Review F01–F05 and F13–F15 with the Malaysian fire-safety, editorial and privacy reviewers.
Supply a rights-cleared fictional scene and numbered text equivalent, the five source hazard-group cards, source heat/fuel framing, reviewed observation cues and contextual feedback.
P7 coil/curtain material may be used only as a clearly labelled composite learning scenario after review; no incident facts or outcome claims have been added.
Verify that the checkpoint requires two supported cues, their conditions and a bounded follow-up; do not invent a universal hazard key.
Blueprint source: CAPAi_Module01_KSDA_Blueprint_v1.0.md, Mission 1. Engine Master Spec v1.0 §§3, 6–8 and 10 govern typed blocks, privacy, approval and completion.

missions.title: Turn a risk into a safer routine
missions.purpose: Turn a noticed condition into one safe, performed routine or a clear request for competent help.
missions.knowledge: Distinguish the six source prevention habit areas and recognise when the next step belongs to a competent person.
missions.skill: Use an approved checklist to describe a current condition and rehearse a clear request or safer routine.
missions.desire: Identify one practical barrier and select a realistic response rather than claim perfect household control.
missions.action: Complete a low-risk checklist/routine trial or a full fictional prevention exercise.

blocks.heading: Practise one routine
body: Choose one routine you can practise today. You are not being asked to repair electrical equipment or buy a product.

blocks.heading: Observe within your responsibilities
body: The task is a low-risk checklist and verbal routine in a safe setting. It does not require device testing, electrical isolation, replacement or battery handling.
If an item needs competent help, leave handling outside the exercise and practise a factual request.

blocks.heading: Separate what you know from what needs help
body: A prevention check can distinguish a known condition, an uncertainty and a condition that needs a competent person.
A useful routine is specific enough to rehearse. It also has a clear limit: noticing a condition does not make you responsible or qualified to repair it.

blocks.heading: Review the condition privately
body: Which conditions are known? Which are unknown? Which need competent help?
Use your own paper or the fictional checklist. Keep any home inventory private.

blocks.heading: Say the safe next step
body: In the fictional no-heat routine, a person is interrupted. Practise how you would pause the routine and state a safe next step within the reference’s limits.
If the next step belongs to someone with appropriate competence, rehearse a clear description of the condition and the help being requested.

blocks.heading: Make the task feasible
body: Is the barrier time, permission, access, cost or uncertainty? Choose a response you can perform safely now.
You can use the fictional exercise without explaining your circumstances.

blocks.heading: Complete and refine the routine
body: Work through the checklist and speak the routine or request. Compare it with the review criteria and revise one unclear part.
One completed practice is enough for this mission’s Action; additional future fixes are optional planning.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: What did you actually do?
What remained uncertain?
What would make the next attempt easier?

actionInstructions: Choose a reviewed low-risk routine and checklist, or the equivalent fictional checklist.
Describe one specific condition and distinguish observation from repair.
Perform the verbal routine or rehearse the factual request for competent help without handling a suspect item.
Review the attempt, correct an unclear part and choose an improvement for next time.
aarPrompts: What did you actually do?
What remained uncertain?
What would make the next attempt easier?
reviewNotes: DRAFT — safety publication approval has not been granted. No completion-awarding checkpoint is supplied by this content asset.
Review F02–F06 and F14: electrical, battery, alarm, clearance and handling boundaries.
Supply the six source prevention-habit cards with their qualifications, accessible checklist, no-heat roleplay and approved self-review rubric.
Do not publish detached “unplug/isolate/replace” shorthand or turn this practice into a legal inspection standard.
Blueprint source: CAPAi_Module01_KSDA_Blueprint_v1.0.md, Mission 2. Engine Master Spec v1.0 §§3, 6–8 and 10 govern typed blocks, privacy, approval and completion.

missions.title: Make the plan fit the people
missions.purpose: Review whether a plan fits the building and people, and make one unresolved assumption visible.
missions.knowledge: Recognise the source plan elements: layout, feasible routes, meeting point, participation and rehearsal; understand building-specific procedure precedence.
missions.skill: Trace a reviewed plan and identify one unresolved assumption.
missions.desire: Test whether the plan works for a visitor or when one familiar person is absent.
missions.action: Complete and revise a private plan review or fictional planning exercise.

blocks.heading: Make the plan usable
body: A useful plan describes what is actually possible. The drawing is a way to think through the arrangement, rather than a universal instruction for every building.

blocks.heading: Respect building-specific guidance
body: Use the existing approved building arrangement or the fictional plan. This exercise does not require climbing, jumping, a locked-exit experiment or entry into smoke.
Keep real layouts, assistance needs and personal details offline. An ordered written description can replace a drawing.

blocks.heading: Five plan elements to review
body: The source planning framework considers layout, feasible routes, a meeting point, participation and rehearsal. Building-specific procedures govern the plan review.
Consider a visitor, a person who needs assistance and the absence of a familiar adult. Mark anything you cannot verify instead of inventing an option.

blocks.heading: A guest and an unavailable route
body: Fictional scenario: a guest is unfamiliar with the layout, and the usual route is unavailable.
What needs to be checked against the approved plan? Which assumption could leave someone unsure?

blocks.heading: Trace, challenge, check
body: Using the fictional plan or your private paper, trace a usable route from the approved arrangement and identify its meeting arrangement.
Flag anything you cannot verify. Then revise one weakness in the plan explanation or note the clarification needed from a competent building-specific source.

blocks.heading: Make room for another person’s perspective
body: Which assumption would leave someone unsure? What would help them understand the plan?
Think privately without entering names, medical details or a home layout.

blocks.heading: Complete one plan review and revision
body: Perform the paper or text review, then revise one identified weakness. For the fictional option, apply the unavailable-route complication and revise your response.
Testing a route physically is not required.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: What did you assume?
What did your review reveal?
What needs competent building-specific clarification?

actionInstructions: Choose an existing approved household/building arrangement or reviewed fictional plan.
Trace the arrangement on private paper or in an ordered text description without physically testing a hazardous route.
Check a visitor or assistance assumption and identify one condition that is unresolved.
Revise your plan explanation or record one clarification to seek. Complete the blocked-route revision if using the fictional exercise.
Review what you assumed and select an improvement.
aarPrompts: What did you assume?
What did your review reveal?
What needs competent building-specific clarification?
reviewNotes: DRAFT — safety publication approval has not been granted. No completion-awarding checkpoint is supplied by this content asset.
Review F07, F08 and F14; qualified fire/building review must address high-rise context, feasible exits, assistance and trapped-response wording.
Supply an approved fictional floor plan, text alternative, building-procedure precedence notice and scenario-specific accepted responses.
Do not introduce an unqualified “two exits from every room” answer key or a compliance claim.
Blueprint source: CAPAi_Module01_KSDA_Blueprint_v1.0.md, Mission 3. Engine Master Spec v1.0 §§3, 6–8 and 10 govern typed blocks, privacy, approval and completion.

missions.title: Rehearse, notice, improve
missions.purpose: Use a calm tabletop rehearsal to find a weakness, correct it and repeat the affected part.
missions.knowledge: Recognise the source elements of a controlled drill and why review matters.
missions.skill: Narrate a scenario with route, accountability and simulated communication, then identify an improvement.
missions.desire: Treat uncertainty as useful information rather than embarrassment or a reason to improvise danger.
missions.action: Perform a tabletop rehearsal, review it and repeat one corrected part.

blocks.heading: Practise for clarity
body: A calm seated rehearsal is valid practice for this awareness mission. The useful result is something you notice and improve.
Use the plan from the preceding mission, or its fictional equivalent.

blocks.heading: Keep the rehearsal announced and inert
body: Do not call an emergency number, produce smoke, use blindfolds, trigger surprise alarms or block exits.
Use fictional information for simulated communication. No real address needs to be entered or transmitted.

blocks.heading: Make roles and communication clear
body: The rehearsal brings together the plan, who is accounted for, a backup-role arrangement and simulated communication.
A role in this tabletop does not authorize anyone to search a dangerous area. Uncertainty is a useful finding to resolve within the approved plan.

blocks.heading: A fictional night-time complication
body: Fictional tabletop: it is 2:13 a.m. and the usual route in the scenario is unavailable.
Use the reviewed fictional plan to talk through your decisions and the simulated communication. Do not dial a number.

blocks.heading: Talk through the plan
body: Explain the plan, who is accounted for and what information the simulated caller would convey.
Compare the attempt with the observation checklist. Notice a confusing instruction, untested assumption or missing confirmation.

blocks.heading: Notice what needs another attempt
body: Which part feels clear? Which part needs another calm rehearsal? This confidence check does not establish emergency readiness.

blocks.heading: Repeat the corrected segment
body: Finish the tabletop, review it and repeat one corrected segment. Record the improvement privately.
Setting a future drill date can follow the practice; the rehearsal and repeat are this mission’s Action.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: What slowed or confused the rehearsal?
Which assumption failed?
What did you change on the second attempt?

actionInstructions: Choose the approved fictional tabletop or a seated review of a real plan within its approved building guidance.
State that this is a practice-only exercise. Keep all communication simulated.
Narrate the plan, accountability and communication using the reviewed checklist.
Identify an observed weakness, change it and repeat that part.
Reflect privately on what changed; there is no speed target.
aarPrompts: What slowed or confused the rehearsal?
Which assumption failed?
What did you change on the second attempt?
reviewNotes: DRAFT — safety publication approval has not been granted. No completion-awarding checkpoint is supplied by this content asset.
Review F07–F09 and F14: scenario, role limitations, safe alternatives and no-live-call boundary.
Supply approved fictional role/call scripts, observation criteria and correction rationales.
Preserve communication from P52 and closing AAR from W11 as distinct parts; do not claim their source routines were identical.
No evacuation time, fear tolerance or physical risk may be rewarded.
Blueprint source: CAPAi_Module01_KSDA_Blueprint_v1.0.md, Mission 4. Engine Master Spec v1.0 §§3, 6–8 and 10 govern typed blocks, privacy, approval and completion.

missions.title: Put judgement before equipment
missions.purpose: Practise equipment label literacy and recognize the limits of a tool and an awareness learner.
missions.knowledge: Explain that suitability depends on exact label, conditions and training, not cylinder colour or a memorised acronym alone.
missions.skill: Locate relevant information on an approved example label and identify missing information or a stop condition in a fictional case.
missions.desire: Recognise that declining unsafe intervention is responsible judgement, not failure.
missions.action: Complete a simulated label-and-boundary review and explain its limits.

blocks.heading: Put judgement before equipment
body: This mission does not qualify you to fight a fire. Practise recognising the limits of a tool and your own authority.
Equipment judgement follows the planning and rehearsal work in earlier missions.

blocks.heading: Keep this a label-and-scenario review
body: The task does not involve live fire, discharge, pin removal or purchasing equipment.
The fictional or approved example label is an equal practice option. Physical equipment practice belongs with a competent instructor.

blocks.heading: Read what the label actually supports
body: Suitability depends on the exact label, conditions and training. Cylinder colour or an acronym alone is not enough to decide.
Distinguish stated suitability and restrictions from information the label does not establish. A missing prerequisite is a limit to acknowledge.

blocks.heading: Locate the information and the gaps
body: On the example label and its text transcription, find the stated suitability and restrictions.
What remains unknown? Explain one limitation without treating a guess as authorization to use the equipment.

blocks.heading: Check the prerequisites
body: Does the fictional case provide every prerequisite in the reviewed reference? Identify what is missing.
Explain the boundary of the decision you can make from the information available.

blocks.heading: Practise declining unsafe intervention
body: Why might someone feel pressured to use a tool? Practise a calm sentence that respects the reviewed safety boundary.

blocks.heading: Complete the review and explanation
body: Complete the sample-label review. Explain aloud or in private writing one limitation and a safe non-intervention choice.
Looking at a safely accessible real label is optional; the example-label task is sufficient.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: What did the label tell you?
What did it not tell you?
What would you avoid assuming next time?

actionInstructions: Use the reviewed example label and readable transcription.
Locate its suitability and restriction fields without operating any equipment.
Identify missing prerequisite information in the fictional case.
Explain one limitation and a bounded non-intervention choice.
Review what the label could and could not establish.
aarPrompts: What did the label tell you?
What did it not tell you?
What would you avoid assuming next time?
reviewNotes: DRAFT — safety publication approval has not been granted. No completion-awarding checkpoint is supplied by this content asset.
Review F10, F11 and F13 with a Malaysian fire-safety reviewer.
Supply a licensed current local label exemplar, its transcription, and the approved decision bank with rationales.
Local fire classes, electrical suitability, service claims, PASS limitations and physical-competence wording remain review-gated.
No universal purchasing chart, new fire-class key or extinguisher-competence certificate is provided.
Blueprint source: CAPAi_Module01_KSDA_Blueprint_v1.0.md, Mission 5. Engine Master Spec v1.0 §§3, 6–8 and 10 govern typed blocks, privacy, approval and completion.

missions.title: Correct a myth. Carry it forward.
missions.purpose: Explain a reviewed correction, improve the explanation and choose a feasible way to continue practising.
missions.knowledge: Distinguish selected source myths from their reviewed contextual correction.
missions.skill: Explain a correction and adapt the explanation after feedback.
missions.desire: Choose a personally relevant practice and a realistic response to one barrier.
missions.action: Complete one teach-back/rehearsal and revise it, then privately plan a next safe action.

blocks.heading: Carry one practised idea forward
body: Finish with an explanation you have actually practised and improved. A future pledge can follow the Action.

blocks.heading: Keep the correction and its limits together
body: A useful correction includes the context in which it applies. Keep smoke, exit and building qualifications attached to the reviewed explanation.
Learning to repeat a phrase is different from explaining why a correction fits a particular scenario.

blocks.heading: Explain why the correction applies
body: Read a selected reviewed claim and its scenario. Explain the correction in your own words, then compare it with the reference.
Keep any important condition or limit in the explanation you practise.

blocks.heading: Try a private teach-back
body: Explain one reviewed correction to a willing person, or to yourself using the fictional listener prompt.
Compare the explanation with the reviewed reference. Improve any point that was unclear or lost an important qualification.

blocks.heading: Choose a feasible continuation
body: Which next step is realistic? What might block it? Choose a safe alternative that fits your circumstances.
A private seven-day plan is optional. You do not need to share an incident, make a public pledge or disclose personal details.

blocks.heading: Repeat the corrected explanation
body: Perform the explanation and repeat it after revision. The revised teach-back is the Action.
Use the private review to choose what to practise next.

blocks.heading: What completion represents
body: Course completion represents CAPAi fire-safety awareness learning and self-declared practice after all required missions are complete.
It does not establish operational competence or accreditation.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: What did your first explanation leave unclear?
What changed?
What will you practise next?

actionInstructions: Choose one source-reviewed correction and its contextual reference.
Explain it to a willing listener or use the solo fictional-listener option.
Compare your explanation with the approved criteria, including the principle’s important limit.
Revise and repeat the explanation.
Consider the private review and optionally plan a next safe practice.
aarPrompts: What did your first explanation leave unclear?
What changed?
What will you practise next?
reviewNotes: DRAFT — safety publication approval has not been granted. No completion-awarding checkpoint is supplied by this content asset.
Review F01, F02, F06–F08 and F12–F15. All scored corrections and public reminders need approval.
Supply a contextual retrieval bank, rationales and fictional-listener prompts. W18’s eight-item key is source evidence only until reviewed.
No source-supported overall pass percentage exists. Do not invent one; critical-item designation belongs to the qualified reviewer.
Resolve source links, rights and placeholders before offering revised W19–24 downloads.
Blueprint source: CAPAi_Module01_KSDA_Blueprint_v1.0.md, Mission 6. Engine Master Spec v1.0 §§3, 6–8 and 10 govern typed blocks, privacy, approval and completion.
DRAFT — no course Start or completion-awarding assessment may be enabled until required procedures, scenarios, rationales, language and rules receive qualified approval.
This asset adapts blueprint text. Source slide/page references are provenance pointers; the source originals were not revalidated during this content extraction.
English is the source language. Safety-critical BM content needs qualified review; do not silently machine-translate procedures.
Time values are author planning estimates, not measured duration or equivalence to the original eight-hour facilitated course.
Action and AAR remain private. AAR prose must never be submitted, persisted, analysed or scored; incomplete text exists in memory only.
Progress requires approved deterministic checks plus performed Action or safe equivalent and private AAR consideration. Reading this draft is not a completion gate.
Medical and emergency scenario cards, answer keys and rationales are intentionally not invented or embedded in this asset.

courses.title: First Aid / CPR / AED Awareness

missions.title: Begin safely. Make the call.
missions.purpose: Replace an undefined expectation to be a hero with a bounded first-response role and a practised fictional call.
missions.knowledge: Explain the awareness/non-accreditation boundary and identify the reviewed public emergency communication route and call-information structure
missions.skill: Give a coherent mock call using fictional location, observed condition and callback information; name a specific helper in a tabletop scenario
missions.desire: Identify a realistic hesitation or accessibility barrier and select a feasible way to participate without shame or disclosure
missions.action: Actually complete one mock call and repeat its unclear part using approved criteria

blocks.heading: Practise a first safe contribution
body: Your task is to practise a first safe contribution and a clear fictional call. Online awareness learning does not establish physical first-aid competence.
You may speak privately or complete a written tabletop exchange. No recording is required.

blocks.heading: This is a rehearsal
body: Use fictional details. Do not place a live emergency call or test an emergency app.
There are no staged falls, surprise incidents or tasks that require touching another person. Keep real medical, contact and address information offline.

blocks.heading: Choose a setting that matters to you
body: Where might this knowledge matter to you? You can use the fictional community hall without naming anyone or disclosing an incident.

blocks.heading: Choose how to take part
body: What might make it difficult to take part? A private written exchange is a valid alternative to speaking aloud.

blocks.heading: Organize the information in a mock call
body: The source call-practice structure uses a fictional location, the observed condition and callback information. Its purpose is a coherent exchange with the simulated operator.
Distinguish what the scenario states from what you do not know. Practise responding to the operator’s follow-up rather than racing against a timer.

blocks.heading: Rehearse the community-hall exchange
body: Using Community Hall A and the fictional details on the call card, speak or write the opening of the mock call.
Respond to the simulated operator’s follow-up. In the tabletop, name a specific helper for the role stated on the card.

blocks.heading: Find and repeat an unclear part
body: Compare your attempt with the call-information checklist. Which information was missing or unclear?
Repeat that part so the next attempt is more coherent. No speed target is required.

blocks.heading: Review the rehearsal you performed
body: The Action is a completed mock call or written exchange, including an answer to the operator’s question and one corrected repetition.
Any confirmation refers to the rehearsal you performed. It is not a record of an actual emergency call.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: Which information was unclear?
What changed in the second attempt?
What will you keep in your next rehearsal?

actionInstructions: Choose the spoken mock call or written tabletop exchange and use only fictional details.
Use the reviewed call card for Community Hall A to rehearse the opening.
Answer the simulated operator’s follow-up without calling a number or activating an app.
Compare the attempt with approved communication criteria and repeat an unclear part.
Reflect privately on the second attempt.
aarPrompts: Which information was unclear?
What changed in the second attempt?
What will you keep in your next rehearsal?
reviewNotes: DRAFT — safety publication approval has not been granted. No completion-awarding checkpoint is supplied by this content asset.
Review R09–R11 and R14, including current Malaysian emergency communication routes and source dates.
Supply approved fictional call cards, operator questions, response criteria and feedback from P45/W41 before enabling the exercise or completion gate.
No telephone number or service/app claim has been inserted. Do not turn rehearsal content into a live telephone link.
Do not present W6’s anecdote as a documented death or request W43 personal/medical data online.
Blueprint source: CAPAi_Module02_KSDA_Blueprint_v1.0.md, Mission 1. Engine Master Spec v1.0 §§3, 6–8 and 10 govern typed blocks, privacy, approval and completion.

missions.title: Recognise the response pathway
missions.purpose: Recognise where a reviewed first-response pathway changes and explain the limits of online recognition practice.
missions.knowledge: Distinguish the response states and scene constraints described in approved DRSABCD source content
missions.skill: Sort approved response labels and explain which information a fictional scene supplies or still lacks
missions.desire: Replace the pressure to know everything with a repeatable method for noticing the next relevant fact
missions.action: Complete an aloud/written scene walkthrough using the reviewed sequence, then repeat the step that was missed

blocks.heading: Notice the decision
body: Notice the decision before you rush to an action. This mission uses a fictional scene to practise what is known, what is uncertain and which reviewed reference applies.

blocks.heading: Keep practice verbal or written
body: Do not practise airway or recovery-position manoeuvres on a person, handle an electrical hazard or switch real equipment for this task.
Physical technique needs qualified guidance. The online task is recognition and a spoken or written walkthrough.

blocks.heading: Look for the next relevant fact
body: A response pathway connects scene information with decisions. Noticing a state change or a missing fact is part of the reasoning.
Online recognition practice cannot establish whether you can perform the associated physical skills.

blocks.heading: Use the reviewed sequence labels
body: Arrange the reviewed labels using the reference when needed. Explain which information each stage asks you to notice.
Use an untimed text sequence if that is easier than moving cards.

blocks.heading: Separate the facts from the unknowns
body: In the fictional office or gym scene, what does the card explicitly tell you? Which fact is still uncertain?
Explain which additional fact could change your interpretation without guessing a missing condition.

blocks.heading: Name your next learning need
body: Which decision can you explain? Which part needs an instructor’s guidance? You do not need to know everything to identify the next question.

blocks.heading: Perform and repeat the walkthrough
body: Talk or write through one fictional scene using the reviewed sequence. Keep the exercise entirely verbal or on paper.
Compare your reasoning with the reviewed criteria, then repeat the part where you guessed or missed a relevant fact.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: What did you notice first?
Where did you guess?
Which fact would change your decision?
What will you check on your next attempt?

actionInstructions: Use one approved fictional scene with the reviewed sequence reference.
Arrange or write the reviewed response labels and identify the scene facts relevant to them.
Perform a spoken or written walkthrough without touching a person or operating equipment.
Identify one uncertainty, compare your attempt with the reviewed criteria and repeat the affected decision.
Consider the private review and choose what to check next time.
aarPrompts: What did you notice first?
Where did you guess?
Which fact would change your decision?
What will you check on your next attempt?
reviewNotes: DRAFT — safety publication approval has not been granted. No completion-awarding checkpoint is supplied by this content asset.
Review R01–R04: governing protocol, mnemonic attribution, response states, sequence and rationale.
Quarantine W16 Q1/W54 electrical-hazard answer under R02 and W16 Q3 recovery-position answer under R03. Neither is reproduced in this asset.
Supply approved labelled scene cards, linear decision text, reference, mandatory state distinctions and an exact reviewed bank before enabling practice checkpoints.
No procedural DRSABCD steps, physical manoeuvre instructions or unsupported pass mark have been authored.
Blueprint source: CAPAi_Module02_KSDA_Blueprint_v1.0.md, Mission 2. Engine Master Spec v1.0 §§3, 6–8 and 10 govern typed blocks, privacy, approval and completion.

missions.title: Understand the CPR–AED team
missions.purpose: Explain how people, a call and an AED fit together while recognising that physical CPR/AED competence needs coached practice.
missions.knowledge: Distinguish the reviewed recognition, CPR-pathway and AED-role concepts; identify which technique details require qualified demonstration
missions.skill: Allocate and communicate source-supported team roles in a fictional collapse scene and describe an approved continuity check
missions.desire: Identify a practical next learning need without mistaking awareness confidence for clinical competence
missions.action: Run a tabletop role handoff, check for an unassigned task and repeat the handoff clearly

blocks.heading: Understand the team
body: This mission practises team communication in a fictional scene. Physical CPR and AED skills need coached practice with appropriate training equipment.

blocks.heading: Keep the handoff on the tabletop
body: Do not perform chest compressions or breaths on a person, or apply a medical device to a person.
You do not need access to an AED, travel to a device or buy training equipment to complete the online role rehearsal.

blocks.heading: Give a role and hear its confirmation
body: A team exchange needs a clear task owner, a clear request and a reply that confirms the request was understood.
An unassigned or unconfirmed role is a useful gap to find during a fictional rehearsal. Role clarity does not demonstrate the ability to perform CPR or use an AED physically.

blocks.heading: A fictional gym scene
body: Use the gym-collapse scene and the source-supported helper role cards. A solo learner can take each role in turn.
Work with the facts and roles on the reviewed cards; flag information that the scene has not supplied.

blocks.heading: Make the handoff explicit
body: Assign the named helper cards, give each clear request and show how the helper confirms it.
Check for an unassigned task or an unclear reply before you repeat the exchange.

blocks.heading: Choose a coached learning need
body: Which physical skill would you want a qualified instructor to observe? Keep this distinct from confidence in the tabletop conversation.

blocks.heading: Repeat the clearer exchange
body: Perform the tabletop exchange twice, speaking aloud or writing privately. Correct an unassigned or unconfirmed role in the second attempt.
No recording or upload is needed.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: Which task had no clear owner?
How did the reply confirm understanding?
What could this exercise not establish about your physical skill?

actionInstructions: Use the approved fictional scene and helper role cards.
Give the requests and play back each helper’s confirmation, aloud or in a written exchange.
Check the allocation against the approved role criteria and identify any gap.
Repeat the exchange with the unassigned or unconfirmed role corrected.
Reflect on what the role rehearsal cannot establish about physical skill.
aarPrompts: Which task had no clear owner?
How did the reply confirm understanding?
What could this exercise not establish about your physical skill?
reviewNotes: DRAFT — safety publication approval has not been granted. No completion-awarding checkpoint is supplied by this content asset.
Review R05, R06, R10 and R16 with a qualified clinical reviewer.
Supply approved CPR-pathway distinctions, age/circumstance qualifications, AED continuity/device language and role cards with explicit criteria.
W18/W25 responses, all clinical diagrams and any media captions/transcripts need review. No new auto-scored clinical key is included.
Technique targets, pad placement and W21 physical performance records are not mandatory self-demonstration tasks.
Blueprint source: CAPAi_Module02_KSDA_Blueprint_v1.0.md, Mission 3. Engine Master Spec v1.0 §§3, 6–8 and 10 govern typed blocks, privacy, approval and completion.

missions.title: Notice when choking changes
missions.purpose: Notice changing scene information and recognise the need for age- and circumstance-specific, professionally reviewed responses.
missions.knowledge: Distinguish the approved recognition states and age/special-circumstance boundaries in source choking content
missions.skill: Notice a state change in a fictional dinner scenario and identify the matching reviewed reference pathway
missions.desire: Address fear of choosing incorrectly through deliberate recognition and seeking qualified practical training
missions.action: Complete a two-stage verbal/text scenario, explicitly describing what changed and checking the selected pathway against approved feedback

blocks.heading: Watch for the change
body: Watch for a change in the scene, not just a label. This mission practises recognising new information in a fictional dinner scenario.

blocks.heading: Do not act out choking techniques
body: Do not practise physical choking manoeuvres on a healthy person, obstruct a throat, perform thrusts or use forceful partner practice.
Infant technique practice belongs with a training doll and a qualified instructor. This task uses verbal or text cards only.

blocks.heading: Keep context with the reference
body: The source distinguishes recognition states and age or special-circumstance boundaries. Those qualifications matter when matching a scene to its reviewed reference.
When a scene changes, identify the new observation before explaining whether the same reference still fits.

blocks.heading: Compare two stages of the dinner scene
body: Read the first state of the fictional family-dinner scenario, then its changed card.
Which observation changed? Which reviewed reference now applies? Explain the difference in words without acting out a technique.

blocks.heading: Notice an assumption before it becomes a guess
body: What makes guessing risky in this scenario? Which age or circumstance detail do you need to keep in view?

blocks.heading: Explain, compare and retry
body: Explain the recognition and its boundary for both scene states. Check the selected reference against the reviewed feedback.
If you missed a change, repeat that stage and name the information you overlooked.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: What new information changed your interpretation?
What assumption did you remove?
Which practical element needs qualified coaching?

actionInstructions: Use the two approved states of the fictional dinner scenario; choose static text cards if preferred.
Describe the first state and the matching reviewed reference.
Read the changed card, explicitly identify what changed and check the reference again.
Compare both explanations with approved feedback and retry a missed distinction.
Reflect privately on assumptions and the practical learning that needs coaching.
aarPrompts: What new information changed your interpretation?
What assumption did you remove?
Which practical element needs qualified coaching?

W31, W32 and the choking portion of W54 remain a linked DRAFT bank; approve exact wording and rationales before any scoring.
Supply two fully specified state-change cards and approved age-labelled references. New branches need their own clinical approval.
No choking treatment sequence or technique instructions have been added.

missions.title: Prioritise an injury response
missions.purpose: Practise recognising priorities and limits across injury cases, then improve safe access to an existing kit or reference.
missions.knowledge: Distinguish source categories, escalation cues and trained-only activities in approved injury references
missions.skill: Compare fictional injury cards and explain which reviewed concern needs attention, what remains uncertain and where help is needed
missions.desire: Identify an ordinary readiness barrier, such as not knowing where supplies or reviewed references are kept
missions.action: Perform one safe kit/reference-readiness check or an equivalent tabletop kit exercise, then correct one identifiable gap

blocks.heading: Control the task you can safely own
body: Practise noticing concerns and uncertainties in fictional injury cases. Then complete a low-risk readiness check or a fictional kit exercise.

blocks.heading: Readiness practice has clear limits
body: Do not treat a live injury, contact blood or body fluids, deliberately expose yourself to heat or cold, or practise bandaging or tourniquets on people.
This task requires no medicine handling, purchase, inaccessible cupboard, home photo or personal medical disclosure.

blocks.heading: Separate concern, uncertainty and readiness
body: The source case families cover bleeding, minor wounds, burns and sprain–shock scenarios. Each case needs enough facts to interpret a reviewed concern.
A readiness check asks whether you can find safe, existing supplies or a reviewed reference. It does not establish a diagnosis or authorize treatment.

blocks.heading: Compare the fictional case cards
body: Use the four untimed injury cards. For each, explain which reviewed concern needs attention, what remains uncertain and where qualified help is needed.
Keep your explanation within the case facts and reference; there is no competition or speed target.

blocks.heading: Identify a readiness barrier
body: What would prevent you from finding a reference or safe supplies? Use the fictional kit option if access is unavailable.

blocks.heading: Check safe access
body: Locate a safe, accessible existing first-aid reference or kit and identify one actual readiness gap.
Alternatively, inspect the fictional kit labels and improve their organization or reference index. Keep any real inventory private.

blocks.heading: Correct one identifiable gap
body: Make a low-risk correction to reference access or organization within your authority, or revise the fictional kit’s organization/reference index.
Review what changed and which uncertainty still belongs with a qualified professional.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: What was hard to find?
What changed after your check?
Which uncertainty should go to a qualified professional?

actionInstructions: Work through the reviewed fictional injury comparisons within their stated limits.
Choose a safe existing-kit/reference-access check or the fictional kit exercise.
Inspect only safe, accessible information and items; do not handle medicines or practise treatment.
Identify one readiness gap and make a safe correction within your authority, or revise the fictional organization/reference index.
Review the result and identify any remaining professional question.
aarPrompts: What was hard to find?
What changed after your check?
Which uncertainty should go to a qualified professional?

Review R08, R10, R13 and R14: medical durations, clinical thresholds, escalation, positioning and trained-only scope.
Supply a neutral fictional kit inventory, four sufficiently specified case cards, accessible references and approved criteria/rationales.
There is no complete source quiz/key for these cases. Do not generate a diagnosis or treatment answer as a key.
Poisoning material P46/W42 is an optional reviewed information-preparation reference only; no treatment procedure or required medical record is included.

missions.title: Rehearse the whole scene
missions.purpose: Integrate attention, communication, reviewed priorities and reassessment in one bounded tabletop rehearsal.
missions.knowledge: Retrieve reviewed roles, boundaries and previously approved decision criteria without rereading whole chapters
missions.skill: Work through a multi-person fictional scene, assign roles, respond to new information and explain a handover
missions.desire: Value corrective feedback and achievable improvement rather than confident performance or dramatic rescue identity
missions.action: Finish one integrated tabletop run, inspect evidence against approved criteria, then repeat the weakest handoff or decision

blocks.heading: Find a gap while the scene is fictional
body: A good rehearsal finds a gap while the consequences are fictional. This mission combines the earlier awareness activities into one tabletop and one targeted repeat.

blocks.heading: Keep the whole scene on paper or in words
body: Do not stage a collapse, make a live call, use a person as a manikin substitute or create a crowd confrontation.
There is no competitive time limit. You can read each role yourself and keep all writing private.

blocks.heading: Recall the useful roles and limits
body: Recall the roles, boundaries and reviewed decision criteria from earlier missions before returning to the reference.
Vocabulary recall can support the rehearsal; it does not replace performing the tabletop.

blocks.heading: A fictional wedding scene
body: Use the fictional wedding scene map or text description. Work only with the supplied facts and approved role cards.
A new-information card changes the scene during the exercise. Notice what the update changes and what is still uncertain.

blocks.heading: Make ownership and confirmation audible
body: Who owns each task? Give the request and its confirmation. A solo learner can take the role cards in turn.
Explain the fictional handover aloud or in private writing; no recording is required.

blocks.heading: Look at what you actually said
body: Point to the requests, confirmations and handover you actually gave. Compare those with the observation checklist.
Identify where confusion began or a task was left unclear.

blocks.heading: Repeat the weakest part
body: Finish the tabletop and repeat the weakest handoff or decision with a correction.
The second attempt is part of the Action. A promise to rehearse later does not replace it.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: Where did confusion begin?
Which role was unclear?
What changed during your second attempt?
What cannot this tabletop demonstrate?

actionInstructions: Use the approved fictional wedding scene and role cards, alone or with a willing partner.
Complete one tabletop run, assigning tasks and confirming the requests.
Respond to the reviewed new-information card and give the fictional handover.
Compare what you actually said or assigned with the approved observation criteria.
Repeat the weakest handoff or decision with a correction, then consider the private AAR.
aarPrompts: Where did confusion begin?
Which role was unclear?
What changed during your second attempt?
What cannot this tabletop demonstrate?
reviewNotes: DRAFT — safety publication approval has not been granted. No completion-awarding checkpoint is supplied by this content asset.
Review R05–R10 and R15 with clinical and instructional reviewers.
Supply reviewed map/text, update cards, observer criteria and rationales. P57/W51 categories are not a clinically validated scoring instrument.
Use no invented 8/10 or clinical-qualification threshold. Correct designated safety-critical misunderstandings through approved supported retries.
W48 mystery case has no uniquely demonstrated solution and must remain unscored. Optional crossword requires clue/grid consistency review.
Earlier community-hall simulation is an alternate card set; it is not a second mandatory integrated rehearsal.
Blueprint source: CAPAi_Module02_KSDA_Blueprint_v1.0.md, Mission 6. Engine Master Spec v1.0 §§3, 6–8 and 10 govern typed blocks, privacy, approval and completion.

missions.title: Make readiness tangible
missions.purpose: Complete one concrete low-risk readiness improvement and identify a realistic next practice step.
missions.knowledge: Explain the distinction between this online completion and accredited/practical training
missions.skill: Use a readiness checklist, identify a constraint and select an achievable alternative
missions.desire: Choose a personally relevant action and a manageable way to maintain learning
missions.action: Complete one concrete readiness task or equivalent simulation now; review its result and identify a next rehearsal

blocks.heading: Leave with one change you have made
body: Choose a readiness task you can complete safely today. The result is a usable improvement or a completed fictional equivalent.
Online awareness completion does not establish physical competence, clinical authorization or accreditation.

blocks.heading: Keep personal information private
body: Do not make an emergency call or test an emergency app. There is no casualty practice or required medical disclosure.
Keep names, addresses, medical alerts and real contact information on your own device or paper; do not submit them.

blocks.heading: Choose a readiness task
body: Choose a safe existing-kit or reference-access check, a private phone-information review without placing calls, or the fictional readiness-card exercise.
The fictional option asks you to revise a readiness card with a missing reference/access label. No purchase, partner or training booking is required.

blocks.heading: Work with what is available
body: What is available to you today? Choose the safe simulation if you cannot perform a real task within its limits.
You do not need to explain personal circumstances or make a public commitment.

blocks.heading: Make and check the improvement
body: Perform the chosen readiness check, identify a concrete gap and make a safe correction within your authority.
For the fictional option, produce a usable revised card offline and check its reference/access label.

blocks.heading: Choose a next short rehearsal
body: After the Action, choose what a future refresher or qualified practical training session could help you practise.
This future plan is optional and does not replace the readiness task you have performed.

blocks.heading: What these activities establish
body: After every required mission and review is complete, the programme records completion of online awareness activities and self-declared safe application.
Coached practical training remains a separate next learning step. This programme does not issue a clinical competence claim.

blocks.heading: Your private review
body: What did you change?
Was it usable when you checked it?
What barrier remains?
What will your next short rehearsal revisit?

actionInstructions: Choose one reviewed readiness option that is safe and available, or use the fictional card.
Perform the task now without placing calls, testing emergency features or entering personal information online.
Identify and correct one gap; for the simulation, revise the missing reference/access label offline.
Check whether the revised result is usable and consider a further improvement privately.
Optionally identify a next refresher or qualified training need after completing the Action.
aarPrompts: What did you change?
Was it usable when you checked it?
What barrier remains?
What will your next short rehearsal revisit?

This asset adapts blueprint text. Source slide/page references are provenance pointers; the source originals were not revalidated during this content extraction.
English is the source language. Safety-critical BM content needs qualified review; do not silently machine-translate procedures.
Time values are author planning estimates, not measured duration or equivalence to the original eight-hour facilitated course.
Action and AAR remain private. AAR prose must never be submitted, persisted, analysed or scored; incomplete text exists in memory only.
Progress requires approved deterministic checks plus performed Action or safe equivalent and private AAR consideration. Reading this draft is not a completion gate.
Medical and emergency scenario cards, answer keys and rationales are intentionally not invented or embedded in this asset.
